correctness.rationale: A complete proof covers all \(n\ge3\) and all starting subsets and leak choices: when both layers have two white vertices no force starts; for a nearly full layer, two eligible cross-layer forcers are exactly necessary and sufficient to survive any one forbidden forcer, with the \(n=3\) exceptional case analyzed separately; disjoint combinatorial counting corrects the overlap of two nearly full layers, and explicit deletion arguments classify inclusion-minimal sets. An independently written graph-dynamics checker exhaustively verified all 21,824 subsets on graph orders \(n=3\) through \(7\), including full and minimal cardinality distributions; these are corroborating finite checks, not a proof of arbitrary \(n\).

value.rationale: The exact one-leak all-budget polynomial is a meaningful reliability statistic for matched-clique sensor networks, and its irredundant minimal-set polynomial fully classifies redundancy under individual disabled forcers for an infinite natural graph family. Despite an unchanged scalar minimum \(n\), robustness reduces the number of optimal sets to exactly two and creates \(2n inom{n-1}{2}\) nonminimum inclusion-minimal configurations of size \(n+1\) for \(n\ge4\). This information is neither a small parameter increment nor the ordinary zero-forcing count.
